summary.text: A 35-year-old G4P3 woman at 28 weeks of gestation attended a routine antenatal checkup. She had been diagnosed with gestational diabetes mellitus at 18 weeks and was on oral glucose-lowering drugs with suboptimised blood sugar profile monitoring, and she had no history of infection, osmotic diuresis or hypoglycaemic symptoms in the pregnancy. The marriage was non-consanguineous, the families had no history of congenital anomalies or syndromes, and her previous pregnancies were uneventful with healthy children.

The symphysial fundal height was 31 cm and foetal parts were difficult to palpate. Transabdominal ultrasound showed polyhydramnios with a deepest vertical pocket of 12 cm, a small foetal abdominal circumference, a stomach bubble reported absent and a stomach bubble noted in the thoracic cavity, a heart pushed to the right and soft markers including cleft lip and abnormal hands. She was referred to an MFM consultant, whose detailed scan found left-side cleft lip, claw hand, rocker bottom feet and a lung-to-head ratio of 0.58, consistent with congenital diaphragmatic hernia. Amniocentesis karyotyping showed a male foetus with trisomy 18.

After the karyotyping result was reviewed, the parents were informed of the diagnosis and prognosis and given the option of expectant management or early delivery with comfort care, and the possibility of foetal demise was discussed. During subsequent follow-up she had symptomatic polyhydramnios with an amniotic fluid index of 43 cm, and an amnioreduction was performed. She delivered by spontaneous vertex delivery at 34 weeks of gestation and the foetus had no signs of life.
